subject: Capacity signal: dedicated GPU sizing & lead-time coordination for AcmeAI
messages:
From: Tim Zhao <tim.zhao@acmeai.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, AcmeAI Procurement <procurement@acmeai.com>
Date: Sat, 18 Apr 2026 12:02:00 -0700
Subject: Planning ask — estimated GPU reserve for Q3 launch

Stephanie / procurement team —

Quick heads-up from our side: AcmeAI has a product launch scheduled for mid-September and the ML workload has grown during the last two months of trials. We are projecting sustained peak throughput that will require ~120 A100/H100-class GPUs to guarantee latency and throughput SLAs (estimated 25k prompt QPS sustained across 3rd-party customers). We want to explore a Redwood Dedicated pool with a hybrid fall-back to cloud burst for spikes.

Two asks: can you give us (1) a reasonable procurement lead-time for an on-prem / dedicated capacity carveout (HW + racks + networking) if we purchase through an OEM, and (2) alternative options for reserving capacity via cloud providers with guaranteed reservation start dates?

We have a firm launch target (2026-09-15). If there are options to phase delivery — e.g., 64 units on-prem + 56 reserved in cloud — we could accept staggered availability, but we'd like a clear plan and dates to trigger our PO and finance approvals next week.

Thank you — please loop in anyone on your side who owns procurement and vendor coordination.

—Tim
Tim Zhao
Head of ML Infrastructure, AcmeAI
Tim.Zhao@acmeai.com

Attachments: none
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Tim Zhao <tim.zhao@acmeai.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 18 Apr 2026 14:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Planning ask — estimated GPU reserve for Q3 launch

Tim — thanks for the clear ask and the launch date. I ran a quick sizing pass with Marcus and Neha this morning and sketched a phased plan (attached). High level options we should decide between:

- Option A (hybrid): 64 dedicated H100 on-prem delivered in July/August + 56 reserved cloud burst capacity on Day 1 of launch.
- Option B (cloud-first): 120 reserved cloud instances with a 4–6 week procurement window — faster but higher steady-state cost.
- Option C (OEM purchase): OEM direct purchase of 120 cards — more capex-efficient at scale but expect 10–12 week lead time plus staging/ops prep.

I attached a preliminary capacity spreadsheet (capacity_prelim.xlsx) with expected sustained tokens, buffer headroom (10%), and short notes on rack/PSU needs. Can you confirm whether AcmeAI prefers on-prem ownership (capex) vs. op-ex reservation? That will change the procurement path.

Next steps I propose: Marcus to solicit formal OEM quotes and lead times; Neha to draft a phased onramp runbook aligned to your SLOs; I will prepare an SOW and timeline for your procurement and finance teams. If you can commit to which option by EOD Apr 23 we can lock vendor holds.

Best —
Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai

Attachment: capacity_prelim.xlsx (sheet: summary, timing assumptions)
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Omega OEM Sales <sales@omega-oem.com>
Date: Sun, 19 Apr 2026 09:35:00 -0700
Subject: OEM options & lead-times (H100 / A100) — initial quotes attached

Stephanie — following up with the vendor intel. I reached out to two OEM channels and got preliminary lead-time windows and a draft quote from Omega (attached: quote_omega_20260416.pdf). Key takeaways:

- Omega (H100-class): currently quoting 10–12 calendar weeks for delivery after PO (they have a regional backlog for Q3). Price estimate in the PDF; includes rail kits and basic support.
- Cloud provider (us-east-1 reserved pool): can guarantee reserved capacity with a 3–4 week provisioning SLA, but requires a 6–9 month reservation commitment for the best pricing tiers — they also offer an initial 8-week warm pool at a premium.
- A100 alternatives shave ~10–15% off unit cost and have 6–8 week lead-times via some resellers, but our performance team warns of model perf differences at scale (Neha will validate).

Suggested procurement plan to meet a Sep 15 launch: place a PO for 64 H100s with Omega by Apr 27 to hit a mid-July delivery window (assuming 10–12 weeks). Simultaneously, reserve 56 cloud instances in a warmed reserved pool with the cloud provider to cover day-one capacity. This reduces risk if OEM slips.

Please note vendor holds are not guaranteed — I requested a written hold but they require a non-binding LOI or deposit to lock the Q3 queue. We should decide on deposit authorization by Apr 23 to keep that path open.

--Marcus
Marcus Lin
Director, Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.ai

Attachment: quote_omega_20260416.pdf
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 Apr 2026 10:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: OEM options & lead-times (H100 / A100) — ops considerations

Quick operational note on the hybrid plan:

- Rack & power: for 64 H100-class cards we need 6–8 full racks depending on vendor chassis density. That adds 2–3 weeks for datacenter scheduling and cable provisioning.
- Network fabric: plan for a transient performance hit if we bring cloud burst and on-prem together — will need careful KV cache affinity routing to avoid cross-host latency. We should include an ops task to validate routing & fallback policies before day-one.
- Warm pool strategy: I support a 10% buffer (12 nodes) called out in the spreadsheet. The cloud provider warm pool for 8 weeks at premiums is a reasonable bridge until OEM hardware arrives.

Budget redline: getting a deposit to hold Q3 queue (~20% of PO) will need an expedited approval from finance — I can draft the CAPEX call-out but we need procurement to commit before Apr 27.

I ran a quick checklist and attached a short onboarding draft (redwood_onboarding-draft.docx) — it lists SRE runbooks, rack mapping, and onboarding SLAs.

-Dev
Dev Patel
Prod Ops Manager, Redwood Inference
dev_patel@redwood.ai

Attachment: redwood_onboarding-draft.docx
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Tim Zhao <tim.zhao@acmeai.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, AcmeAI Procurement <procurement@acmeai.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2026 16:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Planning ask — estimated GPU reserve for Q3 launch

Tim — thanks for the initial signal and the quick reviews internally. Summarizing the recommended, low-risk path and clear asks for your procurement team: 

1) Recommended path (hybrid): place a PO / LOI to cover 64 H100s with Omega (target delivery mid-July) + reserve 56 cloud instances in a warmed reserved pool for day-one throughput. This balances cost and schedule risk.

2) Critical dates: decision on deposit/LOI by Apr 27 to hold the OEM queue; confirmation of cloud reservation by Apr 30 to guarantee warm pool in July-Sept window.

3) Redwood deliverables: we will (a) send an updated SOW + phased timeline by EOD Apr 23, (b) provide the vendor LOI template for finance, and (c) schedule a standing weekly 30-min procurement sync starting Apr 26.

4) Action needed from AcmeAI: confirm preferred procurement path (capex vs. op-ex) and provide PO contact for the deposit authorization. If you want us to pursue a full OEM-only path, we’ll need a faster commit and a ~20% deposit to lock Q3 allocation.

Links: HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/ACME-42 — Draft SOW will be uploaded for signature via DocuSign (https://www.docusign.com/ACME-42/initial-sow).

If that plan sounds acceptable I’ll route the SOW + LOI template to procurement. Happy to hop on a 20-min call tomorrow to walk through timelines.

Best regards,
Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai

Attachments referenced: capacity_prelim.xlsx, quote_omega_20260416.pdf, redwood_onboarding-draft.docx
